issues.description: download_and_untar.sh warns when unzip is missing but does not exit, continuing into broken state
issues.detail: The `command -v unzip` check echoes a message and falls through. Same for the argument validation block: it cats usage and continues. A script that lies about its preconditions is hostile to the next maintainer. Add `exit 1` after both warnings. Bash discipline 101.

issues.description: realpath arguments unquoted; breaks on paths with spaces
issues.detail: `extract_dir=$(realpath $1)` and `zip_dir=$(realpath ${2:-$extract_dir})` lack quotes. Any path with a space silently corrupts. The rest of the script uses quoted expansions correctly, which makes this an inconsistent, easy-to-miss footgun. Quote them: `$(realpath "$1")`.

issues.description: data.sh transcript filtering pipes five sed invocations where one would do
issues.detail: Five chained `sed` calls each spawn a process to strip a single character. This is the kind of pipeline that gets copy-pasted into the next recipe and grows. One `sed -e ... -e ...` or a single `tr -d` does the job and reads cleaner. Not a blocker, but it is bad taste in the linked-list-special-case sense.

issues.description: Symlinks committed without trailing newlines (`No newline at end of file`)
issues.detail: asr.sh, db.sh, path.sh, pyscripts symlinks all show `\ No newline at end of file`. Other egs2 recipes follow the same pattern, so this is style-consistent with the codebase and not worth refusing over — but worth noting because it shows up across four files in the diff and signals copy-from-template rather than thought.

issues.description: Hardcoded utterance counts in data.sh heredoc are brittle and undocumented
issues.detail: `22467`, `3208`, `6072`, `29386`, `38924` appear as magic numbers used to hard-fail data prep. If the upstream dataset shifts by one file, the recipe breaks with no path to recovery. Fine for a reproducibility gate, but the commit message should say so, and the error should tell the user to verify the download rather than assume their code is wrong.

issues.description: README links to a config path that does not exist in the diff
issues.detail: README points to `./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml` but the actual file lives at `./conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml` (no `train/` subdir). Broken doc link on day one. Trivial fix; just wastes the next reader's time when the link 404s.

review.summary: A new egs2 recipe that follows the existing template closely — the symlinks, cmd.sh, queue/slurm configs are boilerplate copies and that's fine, that's how this codebase works. The actual new code is local/data.sh and local/download_and_untar.sh, and that's where the issues are. download_and_untar.sh warns-and-continues instead of failing on missing prerequisites, which is exactly the kind of bug that gets reported six months from now as "the recipe silently skipped extraction." data.sh has a five-sed pipeline that should be one sed, and hardcoded utterance counts with no documentation of why. README link is broken on arrival. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — fix the exit-on-missing-unzip, quote the realpath args, fix the README link, then land it.
